title: Claim decomposition into atomic statements (foundational)
description: Signature original: An answer is split into atomic claims, one verifiable fact per unit, using sentence segmentation followed by clause splitting on conjunctions. Atomicity matters because a single sentence can hide three separate facts, and only atomic claims can be linked one-to-one with evidence. Each atomic claim is stored with its character offsets so the chain can be audited back to the exact wording. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import re
text = 'The archive holds 52,000 databases and grows daily, with each record verified.'
parts = [p.strip() for p in re.split(r'[,.] *and |; |\. ', text) if p.strip()]
print('atomic claims:', len(parts))
for i, p in enumerate(parts, 1): print(i, '-', p[:60])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Evidence Chain Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Evidence linking with support scoring (foundational)
description: Signature original: Each atomic claim is matched against candidate source passages using token-overlap scoring, and every link records a support score between 0 and 1. The support score combines lexical overlap with a bonus for exact numeric or named-entity matches, since numbers and names carry most of a claim's checkable content. Links below 0.35 are flagged as weak and must be reviewed before the chain is accepted. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Evidence Chain Builder, 2026-10-21.

t: Chain gap detection for unsupported claims (foundational)
title: Chain gap detection for unsupported claims (foundational)
description: Signature original: After linking, the builder walks every atomic claim and lists the ones with no evidence link above the acceptance threshold. These gaps are reported as explicit missing-evidence items rather than silently dropped, which is what separates a chain builder from a summarizer. A chain is only complete when every claim is either supported or explicitly marked as an assumption. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
claims = [('c1', 0.82), ('c2', 0.21), ('c3', 0.64), ('c4', 0.05)]
TH = 0.35
gaps = [cid for cid, s in claims if s < TH]
print('supported:', [c for c, s in claims if s >= TH])
print('gaps needing evidence:', gaps)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Evidence Chain Builder, 2026-10-21.

title: Provenance graph of claim-source edges (foundational)
description: Signature original: The full chain is stored as a directed graph: claim nodes point to the source-record nodes that support them, and each edge carries the support score and the match type. Graph storage makes transitive questions answerable, such as which single source underpins the most claims, or which claims collapse if one source is retracted. Standard adjacency lists keep this structure small enough to hold millions of edges in memory. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
edges = [('c1','srcA',0.9),('c1','srcB',0.6),('c2','srcA',0.8),('c3','srcC',0.7)]
from collections import defaultdict
uses = defaultdict(int)
for _, s, _ in edges: uses[s] += 1
print('claims supported per source:', dict(uses))
print('single point of failure:', max(uses, key=uses.get))
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Evidence Chain Builder, 2026-10-21.

t: Chain verification pass before answer release (foundational)
title: Chain verification pass before answer release (foundational)
description: Signature original: Before an answer ships, a verification pass re-checks every link: the source record still exists, its content hash is unchanged, and the support score still clears the threshold. This guards against link rot and silent source edits, two of the most common ways evidence chains degrade in long-lived archives. Any failed check routes the claim back to re-linking instead of shipping a broken chain. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import hashlib
store = {'srcA': 'the archive holds 52000 databases'}
h = hashlib.sha256(store['srcA'].encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
links = [('c1', 'srcA', h, 0.9)]
for cid, sid, want, s in links:
    got = hashlib.sha256(store[sid].encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    print(cid, 'OK' if got == want and s >= 0.35 else 'FAIL')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Evidence Chain Builder, 2026-10-21.
